review_notes: Reviewed the complete 118-line target and the finite-subscheme and Euler-difference lemmas it uses. The support-finiteness and divisor declarations can be generalized independently of the Euler-characteristic theorem; I have not proposed generalizing the latter, whose supporting theorem is stated over ℂ.

findings.excerpt: (p : X ⟶ Spec (CommRingCat.of ℂ)) [IsProper p] (hd : topologicalKrullDim X ≤ 1)
findings.problem: These three declarations require the structure morphism to have target Spec ℂ, although their relevant finiteness argument only requires a field as the base. This excludes divisors constructed by these declarations for proper curves over other fields without a mathematical need in these results.
findings.proposed_change: Add `{K : Type} [Field K]` to the declarations and replace each `(p : X ⟶ Spec (CommRingCat.of ℂ))` with `(p : X ⟶ Spec (CommRingCat.of K))`. Keep `divisor_degree_eq_euler_difference` over ℂ, since its Euler-difference lemma is also stated over ℂ.
findings.benefit: Users can construct the finite-support order function and divisor for proper integral curves over any field, while the existing complex Euler-characteristic result remains unchanged. The proof of finite support still applies, including the case of empty support.
